reason: Equivalent, because the case that separates the two comparisons has already returned. The line above this one answers equal scores with an explicit tie, so by the time execution reaches here the two scores are known to differ. A greater-than and a greater-than-or-equal can only disagree when the operands are equal, and that never happens on this line. The tie itself — that the same score on comparable evidence is a certain answer rather than a refusal — is asserted in section 5.

reason: Equivalent. This guards reading a named weight off the supplied table. Weakening it lets a truthy non-object through — a string or a number — and the lookup then yields undefined, which Number() turns into NaN. That is the same NaN the original produces by taking the other branch, and the line below turns either into the default weight of one. No supplied value produces a different weight.

Indexing a string by a dimension name yields undefined, exactly as indexing the empty object does, so every dimension is recorded as unanswered either way and the scorecard scores nothing. That a scorecard whose scores field is a string produces no score is covered by the garbage inputs in section 7.
